lines.trans: Mei sent hot mint tea and warm almond biscuits for our composer!
Thank you both. Listen while I tap two rhythms on the table.
Does the ending go fast and bright, or gentle and slow?
Manager Zhou's aunt wrote a light dancing beginning, like morning footsteps.
Then in the middle, the melody climbs up like afternoon conversation!
Exactly! So at six in the evening, how should a Friday waltz end?
Warm and unhurried—like friends lingering over their last cup of tea.
Yes! Repeat the opening four notes softly, one octave higher, and come home.
Just hearing you hum it in this glass room sounds wonderful, Teacher Song!
Wait—right in bar twenty-eight, the melody lands squarely on middle D!
The exact silent key Chen is repairing tomorrow morning!
No pressure for poor Chen—the whole song rests on his tweezers!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yī. Changes tone to yí before 4th tone (一个 yí gè) and yì before 1st/2nd/3rd tones (一杯 yì bēi).

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yí yàng. Pairs with 跟/和 in 跟…一样 ('the same as…').

examples.text: 等等，深蓝色的，跟您的一样啊！
examples.trans: Wait—it is dark blue, the same as yours!

examples.text: 哎呀！我跑得太急，包装看着都一样！
examples.trans: Oh no! I was running in such a rush that the wrappers all looked alike!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yì diǎn. Before a noun, means 'a little bit of' (一点糖); after an adjective, 'a bit more' (快一点).

examples.text: 只有一点点牛奶、两个鸡蛋，一点黄油都没有！
examples.trans: Only a tiny bit of milk, two eggs, and no butter at all!

examples.text: 太好了！请加牛奶和一点糖。
examples.trans: Wonderful! With milk and a little sugar, please.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shàng. Used both as a directional verb/complement ('up, onto') and location word ('on top of').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià wǔ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个下午 ('an afternoon').

examples.text: 您尽管看，宋老师。星期一下午大堂暗。
examples.trans: Go right ahead, Teacher Song. Monday afternoon the lobby was dim.

examples.text: 先别对外面透露一个字！让两兄弟先过完这个星期五下午！
examples.trans: Not a single word to anyone outside yet! Let the two brothers have their Friday afternoon first!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xià cì. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 下一次 ('the next occasion').

examples.text: 下次来成都，一定再来住我们客栈！
examples.trans: Next time you come to Chengdu, be sure to stay at our inn again!

examples.text: 今天聊得很开心，我们下次见！
examples.trans: It was lovely chatting today—see you next time!

meanings.note: Pinyin: bù. Standard negation for present/future/habitual verbs and adjectives; shifts to bú before a 4th tone (不是 bú shì).

examples.text: 下雨的时候，纸不会弄丢房间名单。
examples.trans: When it rains, paper will not lose the room list.

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎng. Used instead of 二 when counting things with a measure word (两个, 两把, 两间).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gè. Most common Mandarin measure word (量词), placed between a number/demonstrative and a noun (一个人, 这个).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhōng yāng. Compound 中 ('middle') + 央 ('center'); also used in music for the middle register (中央八度 'middle octave').

examples.text: 院子中央摆着一张干净的木头圆桌。
examples.trans: A clean round wooden table stands in the center of the courtyard.

examples.text: 请把手放在钢琴键盘的中央。
examples.trans: Please place your hands at the center of the piano keyboard.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhōng jiān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 正中间 ('the exact middle').

examples.text: 当然不能偷看……咦，自己翻开在中间那页了！
examples.trans: Of course we must not peek... oh, it fell open to the middle page by itself!

examples.text: 两栋砖房中间是一个安静的小院。
examples.trans: Between the two brick buildings lies a quiet small courtyard.

meanings.note: Pinyin: le. After a verb, marks completion; at the end of a sentence, signals a change of situation.

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: Pinyin: èr shí bā. Cardinal number 二十 ('twenty') + 八 ('eight'); becomes ordinal with 第 (第二十八 'twenty-eighth').

examples.text: 这首曲子的第二十八小节非常温柔。
examples.trans: The twenty-eighth bar of this piece is very gentle.

examples.text: 二月通常只有二十八天。
examples.trans: February usually has only twenty-eight days.

meanings.note: Pinyin: cóng róng. Describes a relaxed, unhurried pace or manner without panic.

examples.text: 宋老师说话的声音总是温和又从容。
examples.trans: Teacher Song's voice is always warm and unhurried.

examples.text: 提前准备好材料，做饭时就能很从容。
examples.trans: When you prepare the ingredients ahead of time, you can cook calmly and unhurriedly.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tā. Third-person singular masculine pronoun; pronounced identically to 她 and 它.

examples.text: 他没要回那个装木头小火车的箱子吗？
examples.trans: Did he not ask back for that case with the wooden train?

examples.text: 他留了纸条，请我们保管到星期五。
examples.trans: He left a note asking us to keep it until Friday.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zuò qǔ jiā. Combines 作曲 ('compose music') + specialist suffix 家 ('master/specialist').

examples.text: 这位年轻的作曲家写了好几首钢琴曲。
examples.trans: This young composer has written several piano pieces.

examples.text: 我最喜欢的作曲家经常从民间音乐里找灵感。
examples.trans: My favorite composer often finds inspiration in folk music.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nǐ men. Plural 'you' for addressing two or more people (including polite groups).

examples.text: 太谢谢你们两位了。
examples.trans: Thank you both so very much.

examples.text: 不怪你们。只是我身上只有这件外套！
examples.trans: It is not your fault. Still, I only have this one coat on me!

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎ. Colloquial fusion of 两个, never followed by 个 (我们俩 'the two of us').

examples.text: 啊！黄色柠檬糖霜——每个星期五我们俩都抢边角那一块！
examples.trans: Oh! Yellow lemon glaze—every single Friday the two of us fought over the corner piece!

examples.text: 别动，你们俩。听到路边汽车停下的声音了吗？
examples.trans: Hold still, both of you. Hear that car engine stopping at the curb?

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiū. Used for fixing pipes, locks, furniture, or appliances (修好 'fix completely').

examples.text: 这么快就修好了？老陈你随身带着螺丝刀啊！
examples.trans: Fixed that fast? Chen, you carry a screwdriver everywhere on you!

examples.text: 听听保养大师说的！昨天修热水器，今天修两兄弟！
examples.trans: Listen to the maintenance master! Yesterday fixing the boiler, today fixing two brothers!

meanings.note: Pinyin: bàng wǎn. Combines 傍 ('draw near to') + 晚 ('evening'): the golden hour around sunset.

examples.text: 傍晚的时候，院子里的灯笼一盏接一盏亮了。
examples.trans: At dusk, the lanterns in the courtyard lit up one after another.

examples.text: 夏天的傍晚最适合坐在院子里乘凉。
examples.trans: Summer evenings at dusk are perfect for sitting in the courtyard to enjoy the breeze.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiàng. Introduces a likeness or example ('look like, be like').

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

examples.text: 他长得真像他哥哥。
examples.trans: He really looks like his older brother.

meanings.note: Pinyin: quán. Emphasizes entirety before 都 or a verb (全都 'every single one').

examples.text: 怪不得这么重，全是木头和皮鞋！
examples.trans: No wonder it was so heavy—all wood and leather shoes!

examples.text: 四张桌子，八把椅子，全摆好了！
examples.trans: Four tables, eight chairs—everything is set in place!

meanings.note: Pinyin: bā dù. Musical interval of eight scale degrees: 八 ('eight') + 度 ('degree/interval').

examples.text: 请把这段旋律升高一个八度再弹一次。
examples.trans: Please raise this melody by one octave and play it again.

examples.text: 钢琴中央八度的音色最温暖。
examples.trans: The tone of the piano's middle octave is the warmest.

meanings.note: Pinyin: liù. Cardinal number 6.

examples.text: 老陈……小晴……快告诉我今晚六号房空着。
examples.trans: Chen... Qing... please tell me room six is free tonight.

examples.text: 没有啊，周经理，南方来的夫妻一小时前住进六号房了。
examples.trans: No, Manager Zhou, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zài. Marks a next step in sequence (先提再推) or a future repetition (再见 'see you again').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiě. Used for writing characters, notes, letters, or reviews.

examples.text: 到星期五？没写名字，也没签名！
examples.trans: Until Friday? No name written, and no signature either!

examples.text: 只剩三十五分钟了！他肯定会写一星差评！
examples.trans: Only thirty-five minutes left! He will surely write a one-star bad review!

meanings.note: Pinyin: chū lái. Directional complement for coming out or figuring something out (认出来).

examples.text: 明信片上整齐的方格字，我两秒钟就认出来了。
examples.trans: That neat block handwriting on the postcard—I recognized it in two seconds.

examples.text: 看合页边露出来的折纸图纸——一楼画着一扇暗门！
examples.trans: Look at the folded blueprint sticking out of the hinge—a hidden door is drawn on the ground floor!

related.gloss: come fresh out of the oven

meanings.note: Pinyin: dào. Works as main verb ('arrive') or result complement ('succeed in reaching/perceiving', 找到, 听到).

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房今天到。
examples.trans: Right, eight guest rooms, eight brass keys. Room four arrives today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shēng. Means 'rise' (太阳升起来) or 'promote' someone to a higher post (升职).

examples.text: 小晴做事认真，经理升她做正式前台。
examples.trans: Qing works conscientiously, so the manager promoted her to permanent receptionist.

examples.text: 太阳升起来以后，石板路很快就干了。
examples.trans: Once the sun rose, the flagstone path dried quickly.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yā lì. Measure word (量词): 种 (zhǒng), e.g. 一种压力 ('a kind of pressure').

examples.text: 坏消息。老热水器上的铜压力阀门裂了。
examples.trans: Bad news. The brass pressure valve on the old water heater cracked.

examples.text: 换了新阀门，三楼的水压没有压力问题了。
examples.trans: With the new valve in place, the upstairs water pressure is steady.

related.gloss: a kind of pressure (measure word 种)

meanings.note: Pinyin: yòu. Marks an action repeating, or pairs two qualities in 又A又B ('both A and B').

examples.text: 真的可以吗？看着又好看又暖和！
examples.trans: Is that really alright? It looks both lovely and warm!

examples.text: 又是深蓝色行李箱！这是宋老师的吗？
examples.trans: Another dark-blue suitcase! Is this Teacher Song's?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǐ. Read zhǐ as the adverb 'only' before verbs, and zhī as a measure word for cups, boxes, and small animals.

examples.text: 而且他坐晚上八点的火车到——只剩四十分钟了！
examples.trans: And he arrives on the eight o'clock evening train—only forty minutes left!

examples.text: 只剩三十五分钟了！他肯定会写一星差评！
examples.trans: Only thirty-five minutes left! He will surely write a one-star bad review!

meanings.note: Pinyin: kě lián. Often used affectionately or playfully ('poor Chen!') as well as genuinely ('pitiful').

examples.text: 可怜的周经理急得连手里的咖啡杯都忘了。
examples.trans: Poor Manager Zhou was so flustered he forgot the coffee cup in his hand.

examples.text: 那只淋了雨的小猫看起来真可怜。
examples.trans: That little cat caught in the rain looked truly pitiful.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tīng. Focuses on the act of listening; add 见 or 到 (听见, 听到) for actually hearing.

examples.text: 老陈，你听到了吗？有人按了大门门铃！
examples.trans: Chen, did you hear that? Someone rang the front gate bell!

examples.text: 我在院子里老远就听到你们喊黄油了。
examples.trans: All the way out in the courtyard I heard you shouting about butter.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ne. After a noun, asks 'what about X?' (你呢？); at the end of a statement, highlights an ongoing situation.

examples.text: 等一下，咖啡厅的小美正朝我招手呢！
examples.trans: Wait a moment—Mei in the café is waving toward me right now!

examples.text: 来成都的第一个晚上，怎么能难过呢！
examples.trans: On your very first evening in Chengdu, how could you sit around sad!

meanings.note: Pinyin: hé. Joins nouns or pronouns ('A and B'), NEVER two whole clauses; also means 'with' (和你一样).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiǎng. Used for bells, phones, pipes, or alarms ringing or clanking.

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hēng. Read 1st-tone hēng when softly humming a tune under one's breath (哼歌 'hum a song').

examples.text: 小美一边揉面团，一边轻轻哼着歌。
examples.trans: Mei softly hummed a tune while kneading bread dough.

examples.text: 宋老师看着旧乐谱，小声哼出了第一句。
examples.trans: Looking at the old score, Teacher Song softly hummed the opening phrase.

meanings.note: Pinyin: la. Colloquial fusion of 了 + 啊 adding cheerful energy at the end of a sentence.

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 你们守着，我出门啦！
examples.trans: Hold the fort—I am heading out the door!

meanings.note: Pinyin: sì. Cardinal number 4.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房今天到。
examples.trans: Right, eight guest rooms, eight brass keys. Room four arrives today.

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

meanings.note: Pinyin: huí jiā. Verb-object compound 回 ('return') + 家 ('home'); takes no location particle between them.

examples.text: 买完菜以后，我们一起走路回家吧。
examples.trans: After finishing the grocery shopping, let's walk home together.

examples.text: 下班回家的路上，我买了一束鲜花。
examples.trans: On my way home from work, I bought a bunch of fresh flowers.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wéi. Often followed by 着 (围着桌子 'gathered around the table').

examples.text: 傍晚大家围着木桌一边喝茶一边聊天。
examples.trans: At dusk everyone gathered around the wooden table drinking tea and chatting.

examples.text: 院子四周用青砖围成了一道矮墙。
examples.trans: Blue bricks form a low wall surrounding all four sides of the courtyard.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yuán wǔ qǔ. Compound from 圆 ('circle') + 舞 ('dance') + 曲 ('musical piece'). Measure word: 首 (shǒu).

examples.text: 宋老师在钢琴上弹了一首轻快的圆舞曲。
examples.trans: Teacher Song played a lively waltz on the piano.

examples.text: 这首老圆舞曲让人想起三十年前的晚茶会。
examples.trans: This old waltz brings back memories of evening tea gatherings thirty years ago.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zài. As main verb/preposition, gives location (在院子里); before another verb, marks ongoing action ('be doing').

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tài. Often frames 太 + adj + 了 for warm exclamations (太好了！ 'Wonderful!').

examples.text: 太好了。请告诉我需要知道什么。
examples.trans: Great. Please tell me what I need to know.

examples.text: 太好了。窗户朝街上还是朝院子？
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

meanings.note: Pinyin: gū gu. Specifically father's sister (second syllable neutral tone); distinct from 阿姨 / 姨妈 (mother's sister).

examples.text: 周经理的姑姑以前也住在这座老院子里。
examples.trans: Manager Zhou's paternal aunt used to live in this old courtyard too.

examples.text: 我姑姑年轻的时候最喜欢弹钢琴。
examples.trans: When my aunt was young, she loved playing the piano most of all.

meanings.note: Pinyin: duì. Means 'correct!' on its own, 'right' as a result complement (拿对), or 'to/toward' before a noun.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房今天到。
examples.trans: Right, eight guest rooms, eight brass keys. Room four arrives today.

examples.text: 看拉链旁边……对，有她的名字缩写！
examples.trans: Check beside the zipper... yes, her name initials are here!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiǎo jié. In music notation, counts bars/measures between vertical barlines (二十四小节 'twenty-four bars').

examples.text: 这首圆舞曲的前八个小节特别轻快。
examples.trans: The opening eight bars of this waltz are especially light and lively.

examples.text: 宋老师用铅笔在第四小节旁边做了记号。
examples.trans: Teacher Song made a pencil mark beside the fourth bar.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiù. Highlights immediacy, exact location (就在这里), or smooth consequence ('then').

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

examples.text: 朝院子，就在老树上面，非常安静。
examples.trans: Toward the courtyard, right above the old tree; it is very quiet.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiù shì. Adds emphatic certainty before a noun ('is the very one').

examples.text: 你好！你就是小晴吧？我是厨房的小美。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Qing, right? I am Mei from the kitchen.

examples.text: 没关系！您就是志豪先生吧？
examples.trans: No problem at all! You must be Mr Zhihao, right?

meanings.note: Pinyin: kāi tóu. Noun (or separable verb) 开 ('open/start') + 头 ('head/beginning').

examples.text: 这首圆舞曲开头的旋律轻快又明亮。
examples.trans: The opening melody of this waltz is light and bright.

examples.text: 故事的开头发生在一个下着大雨的五月夜晚。
examples.trans: The beginning of the story takes place on a rainy night in May.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǎng shàng. Directional phrase 往 ('toward') + 上 ('up'), placed directly before action verbs (往上抬 'lift upward').

examples.text: 先把窗板轻轻往上抬一点，再往外拉。
examples.trans: Lift the shutter slightly upward first, then pull outward.

examples.text: 到了中间部分，圆舞曲的旋律一步步往上升。
examples.trans: In the middle section, the waltz melody climbs upward step by step.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zěn me. Before a verb, asks 'how to do X?' (怎么走) or 'how come…?' (怎么还没来).

examples.text: 我的眼镜怎么会在……哎呀！在我头上！
examples.trans: Why would my glasses be in... oh dear! They are on my head!

examples.text: 宋老师，怎么了？您按了门铃！
examples.trans: Teacher Song, what happened? You rang the bell!

meanings.note: Pinyin: nín. Respectful singular 'you' used with elders, teachers, and guests (您好！).

examples.text: 在您的外套口袋里吗？
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: màn màn. Polite host phrase: 慢慢吃 ('take your time eating'), 慢慢走 ('walk safely').

examples.text: 凉？啊——对！老街水管早上需要慢慢热身！
examples.trans: Cool? Ah—yes! Old-street water pipes need a gentle morning warm-up!

examples.text: 把蓝色转轮慢慢往左拧开——别太快。
examples.trans: Turn the blue wheel open slowly to the left—not too fast.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ. First-person singular pronoun; add 的 for 'my' (我的) and 们 for 'we/us' (我们).

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ men. First-person plural pronoun; add 的 for 'our' (我们的).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

meanings.note: Pinyin: fáng. Measure word (量词): 间 (jiān), e.g. 一间房 ('a room').

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房今天到。
examples.trans: Right, eight guest rooms, eight brass keys. Room four arrives today.

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qiāo. Used for knocking on doors or pipes clanking.

examples.text: 听……街口钟楼开始敲十二下了！
examples.trans: Listen... the clock tower at the end of the street is starting to strike twelve!

examples.text: 十二下敲完了……大门外面街上空荡荡的。
examples.trans: Twelve chimes have finished... and the street outside the gate is completely empty.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhěng. Combines with a measure word to mean 'the entire' (整条街 'the whole street', 整栋楼 'the whole building').

examples.text: 今天四号房的客人住一整个星期，一定要完美！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week; everything must be perfect!

examples.text: 今晚半价，而且一整周早餐免费！
examples.trans: Half price tonight, plus free breakfast all week!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xuán lǜ. Musical melody or tune. Measure word: 段 (duàn, 'passage/melody').

examples.text: 这段钢琴旋律听起来既温柔又熟悉。
examples.trans: This piano melody sounds both gentle and familiar.

examples.text: 哪怕过了很多年，我还是记得那首歌的旋律。
examples.trans: Even after many years, I still remember the melody of that song.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zǎo shang. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个早上 ('a morning').

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

meanings.note: Pinyin: míng liàng. Describes both well-lit spaces and clear, ringing musical tones.

examples.text: 擦掉灰尘以后，九号房变得格外宽敞明亮。
examples.trans: After wiping away the dust, Room Nine became remarkably spacious and bright.

examples.text: 这个琴键弹出来的声音干净又明亮。
examples.trans: The sound played by this piano key is clean and bright.

meanings.note: Pinyin: míng tiān. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 明天一天 ('all day tomorrow').

examples.text: 欢迎来到小院客栈，小晴。明天不会无聊了。
examples.trans: Welcome to Courtyard Inn, Qing. Tomorrow will not be boring.

examples.text: 晚安，小晴。明天早餐见。
examples.trans: Good night, Qing. See you at breakfast tomorrow.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīng qī wǔ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 每个星期五 ('every Friday').

examples.text: 我念念：对不起拿错了，请帮我保管到星期五。
examples.trans: Let me read it: Sorry for taking the wrong one; please keep mine until Friday.

examples.text: 到星期五？没写名字，也没签名！
examples.trans: Until Friday? No name written, and no signature either!

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì. Links two nouns (我是小晴); do NOT use simple 是 before plain adjectives like 好 or 忙.

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 有道理！这些是钥匙吗？
examples.trans: Fair enough! Are these the keys?

meanings.note: Pinyin: qǔ zi. Conversational word for an instrumental piece or song tune (second syllable neutral tone). Measure word: 首 (shǒu).

examples.text: 这首轻快的小曲子是姑姑年轻时手写的。
examples.trans: This lively little tune was handwritten by my aunt when she was young.

examples.text: 吃完晚饭，宋老师常在阳光房弹两首曲子。
examples.trans: After dinner, Teacher Song often plays a couple of pieces in the sunroom.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zuì hòu. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 最后一个 ('the last one').

examples.text: 上楼梯，平台往左拐，最上面最后一扇门。
examples.trans: Up the stairs, turn left at the landing, last door at the very top.

examples.text: 冬天用掉最后一个了。只有桥那边的老五金店有这个尺寸。
examples.trans: Used the last one in winter. Only the old hardware shop past the bridge carries this size.

meanings.note: Pinyin: péng you. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个朋友 ('a friend').

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

examples.text: 今天有两位老朋友从外地来看我。
examples.trans: Two old friends are visiting me from out of town today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xìng rén. Combines 杏 ('apricot/almond') + 仁 ('nut kernel').

examples.text: 小美端来了一盘刚出炉的温热杏仁饼干。
examples.trans: Mei brought over a plate of warm almond biscuits fresh from the oven.

examples.text: 用杏仁粉做的柠檬挞底吃起来特别香酥。
examples.trans: A lemon tart crust made with ground almonds tastes wonderfully crisp and nutty.

杯.gloss: measure word for cups and glasses

meanings.en: measure word for cups and glasses
meanings.note: Pinyin: bēi. Counts cups of tea, coffee, water, or juice (一杯热茶 'a cup of hot tea').

examples.text: 太客气了，周经理。半杯就好。
examples.trans: How polite of you, Manager Zhou. Half a glass is fine.

examples.text: 坐下吧，小晴！早上你跑了半条街，喝杯咖啡。
examples.trans: Sit down, Qing! You ran half the street this morning—drink a cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jí le. Follows directly after an adjective to boost it to the max (棒极了！ 'amazing!', 热极了 'super hot!').

examples.text: 等等，咸黄油配果酱不行，做炒蛋却棒极了！
examples.trans: Wait—salted butter fails with jam, yet for scrambled eggs it is amazing!

examples.text: 这是我这个月睡得最香的一晚，洗澡水也热极了！
examples.trans: Best sleep I have had all month, and the shower water was wonderfully hot!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhuō zi. Measure word (量词): 张 (zhāng), e.g. 一张桌子 ('a table').

examples.text: 周经理早！桌子很干净，钥匙也准备好了。
examples.trans: Morning, Manager Zhou! The desk is clean, and the keys are ready too.

examples.text: 老板，看一下桌子后面的镜子。
examples.trans: Boss, take a look in the mirror behind the desk.

meanings.note: Pinyin: huān kuài. Combines 欢 ('joyful') + 快 ('brisk/lively'), especially for upbeat rhythms and melodies.

examples.text: 这首曲子的结尾应该用欢快的节奏，还是温柔的节奏？
examples.trans: Should the ending of this piece use a brisk, cheerful rhythm or a gentle one?

examples.text: 院子里传来了孩子们欢快的笑声。
examples.trans: Cheerful laughter of children drifted from the courtyard.

meanings.en: just right; happen to; right on the dot
meanings.note: Pinyin: zhèng hǎo. Marks a lucky coincidence or exact fit.

examples.text: 大门口正好来了一辆出租车。
examples.trans: A taxi has just pulled up right at the front gate.

examples.text: 他拿旧阀门比对了——架子上正好还剩两个！
examples.trans: He matched it against the old valve—he has two left on the shelf!

段.gloss: measure word for sections, passages, or stretches

meanings.en: measure word for sections, passages, or stretches
meanings.note: Pinyin: duàn. Counts musical passages (一段开头 'an opening section'), paragraphs, road stretches, or periods of time.

examples.text: 周经理的姑姑写了一段轻快明亮的圆舞曲开头。
examples.trans: Manager Zhou's aunt wrote a light, bright opening passage for the waltz.

examples.text: 从客栈走到老集市只有一小段路。
examples.trans: From the inn to the old market is only a short stretch of road.

meanings.en: not have; there is not; did not
meanings.note: Pinyin: méi yǒu. Negates 有 ('have / there is') and past actions.

examples.text: 可惜没有电话号码，只有两个字母和老街名字。
examples.trans: Unfortunately there is no phone number, only two letters and an old street name.

examples.text: 还没有吗？请记下我们客栈的电话和地址，谢谢！
examples.trans: Not yet? Please write down our inn's phone number and address, thank you!

meanings.note: Pinyin: méi cuò. Enthusiastic agreement ('Spot on! / Exactly!').

examples.text: 没错！你已经很习惯这儿了。
examples.trans: Exactly! You already fit right in here.

examples.text: 没错。外面大街很吵，进了院子却只听见树叶和小鸟。
examples.trans: Exactly. Outside on the main road it is noisy, yet inside the courtyard you only hear leaves and birds.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wēn nuǎn. Warmer and more emotional than plain 暖; used for sunshine, sound, and kindness.

examples.text: 听……有点低，很温暖，等等——中间这个琴键没有声音！
examples.trans: Listen... a little low, very warm, and wait—this middle key makes no sound!

examples.text: 谢谢你，你的话让我很温暖。
examples.trans: Thank you, your words make me feel warm inside.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wēn róu. Describes a gentle melody, warm voice, or kind manner.

examples.text: 这首圆舞曲的开头温柔得像春天的微风。
examples.trans: The opening of this waltz is as gentle as a spring breeze.

examples.text: 宋老师说话的声音总是很温柔。
examples.trans: Teacher Song's speaking voice is always gentle and warm.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wēn rè. Combines 温 ('mildly warm') + 热 ('hot'): gently warm to the touch or taste without burning.

examples.text: 盘子里装着刚出炉、还带着温热的杏仁饼干。
examples.trans: On the plate are freshly baked almond biscuits that are still warm.

examples.text: 喝一口温热的薄荷茶，整个人都放松下来了。
examples.trans: After a sip of warm mint tea, you feel completely relaxed.

meanings.note: Pinyin: diǎn. Marks hours on the clock (八点 'eight o'clock') or 'a bit' (一点).

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: 晚上九点？你站这儿，我们一起去开门。
examples.trans: Nine in the evening? Stay right here; let us go open the gate together.

meanings.note: Pinyin: rè. Describes hot tea, hot water, or warm weather.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: rán hòu. Connects sequential events across clauses.

examples.text: 过桥，右边经过绿药店。然后呢？
examples.trans: Cross the bridge, green pharmacy on the right. And after that?

examples.text: 先把门把手往上提，然后再往里推。
examples.trans: Lift the door handle upward first, and then push inward.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bō li. Measure word (量词): 块 (kuài), e.g. 一块玻璃 ('a pane of glass').

examples.text: 小晴，隔着玻璃看——他们俩在树下面对面站着呢！
examples.trans: Qing, look through the glass—the two of them are standing face to face under the tree!

examples.text: 擦干净玻璃窗以后，屋里亮多了。
examples.trans: After wiping the glass window clean, the room is much brighter.

related.gloss: a pane of glass (measure word 块)

meanings.note: Pinyin: qín jiàn. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个琴键 ('a piano key').

examples.text: 小晴，你看这些白琴键，又干净又完整。
examples.trans: Qing, look at these white keys—clean and whole.

examples.text: 听……有点低，很温暖，等等——中间这个琴键没有声音！
examples.trans: Listen... a little low, very warm, and wait—this middle key makes no sound!

meanings.note: Pinyin: ruì yīn. Combines Chinese solfège 瑞 (ruì, 'Re / D') + 音 ('musical note').

examples.text: 第二十八小节的旋律正好稳稳落在中央瑞音上！
examples.trans: The melody in bar twenty-eight lands squarely on middle D!

examples.text: 修好轴销以后，中央瑞音终于重新发出了清脆的声音。
examples.trans: Once the hinge pin was fixed, middle D finally rang out clearly again.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Links modifiers or owners to nouns (我的书 'my book', 安静的院子 'quiet courtyard').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhe. Placed right after a verb to show a state or posture continues (门开着 'the door stands open').

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

examples.text: 白纸包着什么？一个木头小火车！
examples.trans: What is wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǒng. Read zhǒng as a measure word for kinds/types (这种, 那种); read zhòng as the verb 'plant/grow'.

examples.text: 老陈，这些香草是你自己种的吗？
examples.trans: Chen, did you grow these herbs yourself?

examples.text: 老房子连着旧回忆——那种争吵最伤人。
examples.trans: Old houses are tied to old memories—arguments like that cut deepest.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wén wěn. Reduplicated adverb describing steady hands or footing.

examples.text: 火苗亮了——稳稳的蓝火，正合适。
examples.trans: The flame is lit—steady blue fire, right as it should be.

examples.text: 她双手稳稳地端起盛满热茶的托盘。
examples.trans: With both hands she lifted the tray of hot tea steadily.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dì. Placed before any number to turn it into an ordinal (第一 'first', 第二天 'the second day').

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: děng deng. Urgent or casual reduplication of 等 ('wait!').

examples.text: 等等，深蓝色的，跟您的一样啊！
examples.trans: Wait—it is dark blue, the same as yours!

examples.text: 等等，这条街就在附近，走过去只要五分钟！
examples.trans: Wait—that street is right nearby, only five minutes on foot!

结尾.gloss: ending; finale (of a song, book, or film)

meanings.en: ending; finale (of a song, book, or film)
meanings.note: Pinyin: jié wěi. Noun 结 ('tie up/conclude') + 尾 ('tail/end').

examples.text: 这首星期五圆舞曲的结尾应该温暖又从容。
examples.trans: The ending of this Friday waltz should feel warm and unhurried.

examples.text: 故事的结尾让每个人都露出了微笑。
examples.trans: The ending of the story brought a smile to everyone's face.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jié shù. Verb meaning to come to an end or finish an event/piece.

examples.text: 到了傍晚六点，这首圆舞曲该怎么结束呢？
examples.trans: When six in the evening arrives, how should this waltz end?

examples.text: 星期五的音乐会将在晚上九点温暖结束。
examples.trans: Friday's concert will come to a warm close at nine in the evening.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gěi. As main verb, 'give'; as preposition/complement, marks the recipient (给你 'for/to you', 递给我 'pass to me').

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Pinyin: huǎn màn. Combines 缓 ('unhurried/gradual') + 慢 ('slow').

examples.text: 圆舞曲的最后几小节节奏温柔缓慢。
examples.trans: The final few bars of the waltz have a gentle, slow tempo.

examples.text: 乌云在傍晚的天空上缓慢地移动。
examples.trans: Dark clouds drifted slowly across the evening sky.

meanings.note: Pinyin: měi. Core stative adjective for visual, musical, or atmospheric beauty (美极了 'sounds/looks wonderful!').

examples.text: 在这间玻璃房里听您轻轻哼出旋律，真是美极了！
examples.trans: Hearing you hum the melody softly in this glass room is truly wonderful!

examples.text: 傍晚亮起灯笼的小院子特别美。
examples.trans: The little courtyard lit with lanterns at dusk is especially beautiful.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lǎo. Describes longtime friends, historic lanes, or warm respect before a colleague's surname (老陈).

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

examples.text: 所以老房子自己会打招呼？
examples.trans: So the old house says hello by itself?

meanings.note: Pinyin: liáo tiān. Separable verb-object compound 聊 ('chat') + 天 ('sky/day's topics').

examples.text: 中段的旋律一步步往上升，就像老朋友下午聊天一样。
examples.trans: The middle melody climbs upward like old friends chatting in the afternoon.

examples.text: 客人们喜欢坐在院子树下喝茶聊天。
examples.trans: Guests love sitting under the courtyard tree drinking tea and chatting.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiǎo bù shēng. Measure word (量词): 阵, e.g. 一阵脚步声 ('the sound of footsteps').

examples.text: 快点——我刚听到二楼楼梯有脚步声！
examples.trans: Hurry—I just heard footsteps on the second-floor stairs!

examples.text: 木楼梯上传来轻轻的脚步声。
examples.trans: Light footsteps sounded on the wooden stairs.

related.gloss: the sound of footsteps (measure word 阵)

舍不得.gloss: be reluctant to part with; linger fondly

meanings.en: be reluctant to part with; linger fondly
meanings.note: Pinyin: shě bu de. Idiomatic potential compound 舍 ('give up/leave') + 不得 ('cannot bear to').

examples.text: 好朋友围着最后一杯热茶聊天，谁都舍不得走。
examples.trans: Good friends gathered around their last cup of hot tea, reluctant to leave.

examples.text: 这盘柠檬挞太香了，老陈都舍不得一口吃完。
examples.trans: This plate of lemon tart is so fragrant that Chen couldn't bear to finish his slice in one bite.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jié zòu. Combines 节 ('metrical beat/joint') + 奏 ('play music').

examples.text: 宋老师用手指在木桌上轻轻敲出了两种节奏。
examples.trans: Teacher Song lightly tapped out two rhythms with her fingers on the wooden table.

examples.text: 圆舞曲有着轻盈好听的三拍子节奏。
examples.trans: A waltz has a graceful, lilt-like three-beat rhythm.

meanings.note: Pinyin: chá. Measure word (量词): 杯 (bēi), e.g. 一杯茶 ('a cup of tea').

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 先喝杯热茶，吃个肉桂卷坐十分钟吧！
examples.trans: Have a cup of hot tea and a cinnamon roll for ten minutes first!

related.gloss: a cup of tea (measure word 杯)

meanings.note: Pinyin: luò. Used both literally for raindrops/leaves falling and musically for a phrase landing on a note (落在中央瑞音上).

examples.text: 到了第二十八小节，整段旋律稳稳落在了中央瑞音上。
examples.trans: In bar twenty-eight, the whole melody lands squarely on middle D.

examples.text: 几片金黄的梧桐叶轻轻落在院子的石桌上。
examples.trans: Several golden plane-tree leaves drifted gently down onto the courtyard stone table.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bò he chá. Measure word (量词): 壶, e.g. 一壶薄荷茶 ('a pot of mint tea').

examples.text: 宋老师，给您热薄荷茶和蜂蜜。
examples.trans: Teacher Song, here is hot mint tea and honey for you.

examples.text: 晚饭后喝一壶热薄荷茶最助眠了。
examples.trans: A pot of hot mint tea after dinner helps you sleep soundly.

related.gloss: a pot of mint tea (measure word 壶)

meanings.en: want; need; will / be going to
meanings.note: Pinyin: yào. Direct verb for ordering/requesting ('want'), obligation ('need to'), or imminent future (要下雨了).

examples.text: 今天四号房的客人住一整个星期，一定要完美！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week; everything must be perfect!

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiàn. Appears in farewells (再见, 明天见) and as result complement of perception (看见, 听见).

examples.text: 晚安，小晴。明天早餐见。
examples.trans: Good night, Qing. See you at breakfast tomorrow.

examples.text: 老陈，听得见吗？我刚经过绿药店！
examples.trans: Chen, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

meanings.en: should; ought to; be someone's turn
meanings.note: Pinyin: gāi. Short everyday form of 应该 ('should').

examples.text: 电线本来就该拉直了。正常保养，别多想。
examples.trans: The wire needed straightening anyway. Routine maintenance—don't read into it.

examples.text: 热茶和柠檬蛋糕！小晴，你该给紧张的弟弟开个学校。
examples.trans: Hot tea and lemon cake! Qing, you ought to open a school for nervous brothers.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiè xie. Standard expression of gratitude; takes an optional person after it (谢谢您).

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zǒu. Means 'walk' (走路, 直走) or 'leave / head off' (我先走了).

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 从这儿往里走。我帮您把蓝色行李箱提上去。
examples.trans: Walk inward from here. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tiào yuè. Combines 跳 ('jump') + 跃 ('leap'), often describing lively, dancing musical figures.

examples.text: 圆舞曲的开头轻快跳跃，就像清晨院子里的脚步声。
examples.trans: The waltz's opening is light and dancing, like morning footsteps in the courtyard.

examples.text: 阳光透过树叶，在干净的木地板上轻轻跳跃。
examples.trans: Sunlight filters through the leaves and dances lightly across the clean wooden floor.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qīng kuài. Combines 轻 ('light') + 快 ('brisk/lively'), used for footsteps, melodies, or moods.

examples.text: 姑姑写的圆舞曲开头十分轻快，让人一听就想微笑。
examples.trans: The waltz opening written by his aunt is brisk and light, making you smile right away.

examples.text: 忙完一天的活儿，大家迈着轻快的脚步回客栈喝汤。
examples.trans: After a day's work, everyone walked back to the inn with light steps for hot soup.

meanings.note: Pinyin: qīng qīng. Reduplication of 轻 ('light/soft'), used directly before short verbs or with 地 (轻轻地抽出来).

examples.text: 宋老师用两根手指把旧乐谱轻轻抽了出来。
examples.trans: Teacher Song gently slid the old music sheet out with two fingers.

examples.text: 怕吵醒午睡的客人，小晴轻轻关上了木门。
examples.trans: So as not to wake guests napping at noon, Qing closed the wooden door softly.

meanings.note: Pinyin: hái shi. Joins choices in questions (茶还是咖啡？ 'tea or coffee?') or means 'still'.

examples.text: 太好了。窗户朝街上还是朝院子？
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

examples.text: 宋老师早！您想喝咖啡还是红茶？
examples.trans: Morning, Teacher Song! Would you like coffee or black tea?

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhè. Proximal demonstrative; pairs with a measure word before nouns (这个 'this one', 这间房 'this room').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sòng lái. Directional compound 送 ('deliver/bring') + 来 ('toward speaker').

examples.text: 小美特意给宋老师送来了热薄荷茶和杏仁饼干。
examples.trans: Mei specially sent over hot mint tea and almond biscuits for Teacher Song.

examples.text: 街坊花店早上给客栈送来了一篮新鲜黄玫瑰。
examples.trans: This morning the neighborhood flower shop brought over a basket of fresh yellow roses.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nà. Distal demonstrative before measure words (那个 'that one'); at clause start, means 'then / well then'.

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nà me. Opens a conclusion drawn from what was just said (那么，门在哪儿？ 'So where is the door?'); before an adjective it means 'that (much)'.

examples.text: 那么，那些旧书后面有第九扇门！
examples.trans: So behind those old books, there's a ninth door!

examples.text: 那么小美的咖啡馆和宋老师的钢琴，不会吵醒楼上的客人吧？
examples.trans: So Mei's café and Teacher Song's piano won't wake the guests upstairs?

meanings.note: Pinyin: dōu. Summarizes everything BEFORE it and always stands directly before the verb/adjective (我们都喜欢).

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lǐ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 里面 ('the inside').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 在您的外套口袋里吗？
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?

meanings.note: Pinyin: chóng fù. Note polyphone 重 reads 2nd-tone chóng ('again/layer') here, NOT zhòng ('heavy').

examples.text: 结尾高一个八度轻轻重复开头的四个音符，听起来真温暖。
examples.trans: Repeating the opening four notes softly one octave higher at the end sounds so warm.

examples.text: 没听清楚的话，请让我再慢慢重复一遍。
examples.trans: If you didn't catch that clearly, let me repeat it slowly once more.

meanings.note: Pinyin: niè zi. Combines 镊 ('pinch with fine tongs') + noun suffix 子.

examples.text: 整首圆舞曲的中央瑞音，现在全靠老陈手里那把细镊子啦！
examples.trans: Middle D for the whole waltz now rests on that pair of fine tweezers in Chen's hand!

examples.text: 修手表和修钢琴一样，都离不开顺手的细尖镊子。
examples.trans: Repairing watches, just like repairing pianos, relies on fine-tipped tweezers.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiān. Counts rooms of all kinds: bedrooms, guest rooms, studies, kitchens (一间客房 'a guest room').

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房今天到。
examples.trans: Right, eight guest rooms, eight brass keys. Room four arrives today.

examples.text: 那间向阳的旧阁楼书房……快跟我来！
examples.trans: That sunny old attic study... follow me, quickly!

meanings.en: lean against; be next to; rely on
meanings.note: Pinyin: kào. Describes sitting by the window (靠窗) or relying on luck (全靠运气).

examples.text: 全靠运气——加上星期一早上火车上拿错的蓝色行李箱！
examples.trans: Pure luck—plus one swapped blue suitcase on Monday morning's train!

examples.text: 她喜欢坐在靠窗的安静位置。
examples.trans: She likes sitting in the quiet spot by the window.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yīn fú. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个音符 ('a musical note').

examples.text: 安静极了！他坐在第三级台阶上，听每一个音符。
examples.trans: So quiet! He sat on the third step, listening to every single note.

examples.text: 旧乐谱上的每一个音符都是手写的。
examples.trans: Every musical note on the vintage score was written by hand.

meanings.note: Pinyin: bǐng gān. Combines 饼 ('flat baked cake') + 干 (gān, 'dry'): dry baked biscuits or cookies.

examples.text: 小美烤了一盘温热酥脆的杏仁饼干配薄荷茶。
examples.trans: Mei baked a tray of warm, crisp almond biscuits to go with mint tea.

examples.text: 把剩下的饼干收进铁盒里，明天吃还是脆的。
examples.trans: Store the remaining biscuits in a tin so they stay crisp tomorrow.

首.gloss: measure word for songs and poems

meanings.en: measure word for songs and poems
meanings.note: Pinyin: shǒu. Counts songs, poems, and pieces of music (一首歌 'a song').

examples.text: 老陈，好好修一次老钢琴，它会记得每一首歌。
examples.trans: Chen, repair an old piano properly once, and it will remember every song.

examples.text: 宋老师给我们弹了一首老歌。
examples.trans: Teacher Song played an old song for us.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gāo. Describes tall people, high ceilings, or high scores.

examples.text: 让我好好看看你，志豪！你长得比钢琴还高了！
examples.trans: Let me look at you properly, Zhihao! You grew taller than the piano!

examples.text: 我手在发抖——车上下来穿深灰色外套的高个子男人吗？
examples.trans: My hands are shaking—is a tall man in a dark grey coat stepping out?
